verses.text: After the Sabbath, just as the first day of the week was dawning, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to see the tomb.
Suddenly, the ground shook hard. An angel of the Lord came down from heaven, rolled the stone away from the entrance, and sat on it.
His appearance flashed like lightning, and his clothes were white as snow.
The guards shook with fear and froze up like dead men.
The angel told the women, “Don’t be afraid. I know you’re looking for Jesus, the one they crucified.
“He isn’t here—he has risen, just like he said! Come see the spot where he was lying.
“Now move quickly and tell his disciples: ‘He has risen from the dead, and he’s going ahead of you to Galilee. You’ll see him there.’ That’s the message I came to give you.”
The women hurried away from the tomb—scared, but overflowing with joy—and ran to tell the disciples.
Then, suddenly, Jesus met them. “Greetings!” he said. They came up, held on to his feet, and worshiped him.
Jesus told them, “Don’t be afraid. Go tell my brothers to head for Galilee. They’ll see me there.”
While the women were on their way, some of the guards went into the city and reported everything that had happened to the chief priests.
The priests met with the elders, came up with a plan, and paid the soldiers a large amount of money.
They told them, “Say this: ‘His disciples came at night and stole him while we were asleep.’
“If the governor hears about it, we’ll talk to him and make sure you don’t get blamed.”
The soldiers took the money and did what they were told. That story spread among the Jews and is still being told today.
The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had told them to meet him.
When they saw him, they bowed down and worshiped him, though some still had doubts.
Jesus came up and told them, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.
“So go and make disciples among every nation. Baptize them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
“Teach them to obey everything I commanded you. And remember, I’m with you always, right up to the end of the age.” Amen.
